title: Starting a family
body: Our energy story starts here — a young family in a new home. Before solar, before smart thermostats, every kilowatt came straight from the grid. We are heads down parenting and not thinking about energy much.

title: Peak Grid Consumption
body: The mid-2000s were our highest-usage years, regularly topping 1,000 kWh in summer months. We're deep into the toddler years but starting to take notice of high energy bills.

title: New AC and air sealing
body: We replaced our old roof AC unit out of necessity, start air sealing, and installed programmable thermostats. This house is 100 years old and things are leaking.

title: Going Solar
body: Everything changed when solar panels went on the roof. Grid consumption plummeted almost overnight. The meters started running backward in spring and fall — months where our panels produced more than we consumed.

title: First Net Export
body: April 2013: for the first time, our monthly meter reading went negative. We sent 291 kWh back to the grid — more than we used. A small milestone, but it felt like the future.

title: Finding a Rhythm
body: By the mid-2010s, our energy pattern had settled into a new normal. Low grid usage most of the year, with modest draws in the hottest and coldest months. The panels were quietly doing their work.

title: Recent Years
body: The last few years have brought new patterns. Some months crept back up — new equipment, changing habits, life evolving. But the overall arc remains: dramatically less grid dependence than where we started.

title: Looking Back
body: Twenty-two years of data tell a clear story: from 11,000+ kWh per year to under 3,000. From complete grid dependence to months of net export. Our home's relationship with energy was transformed.
